dedupe_keys.name: nist world trade center building collapse investigation

description: After the collapse of the World Trade Center buildings on 11 September 2001, which killed 2,749 people including 400 emergency responders, NIST carried out a federal investigation into why the buildings collapsed, how occupants evacuated and how the emergency response worked, under the National Construction Safety Team Act of 2002. More than 200 professionals, including 85 NIST staff, took part; evidence included interviews with 1,056 surviving occupants and 116 responders, reviews of design, construction and maintenance documents, examination of hundreds of steel components and thousands of video, photo and audio records. NIST held 23 public meetings, had drafts reviewed by an external advisory committee, and released 43 final reports on the towers in October 2005 and three on WTC 7. Coverage: the WTC towers and WTC 7 in New York City. Access: the NIST investigation pages and final reports. Licence: U.S. government work; free. Caveats: the investigation is complete, and underlying evidence collections are not a single open dataset. Simulation uses are as a benchmark for fire-induced progressive collapse, tall building evacuation and responder communication studies. Related records: the NIST Champlain Towers South investigation and NIST Fire Dynamics Simulator.

name: NIST World Trade Center building collapse investigation
outcomes: NIST released 43 final reports on the WTC towers, about 10,000 pages, on 26 October 2005, and three reports on WTC 7; its findings led to more than 40 changes to International Code Council building codes, including exit stairwells, emergency elevators, fire-resistive materials, fire protection and structural resistance to collapse, and 15 changes to NFPA fire standards.
